builds.one_line: Restrained, token-correct snackbar with a genuinely useful hairline auto-dismiss progress bar; the one real proportion question is that Undo (16px/weight 500/accent orange) reads louder than the plain-weight 16px confirmation message it's attached to.
builds.proportion: Confirmation message "Change saved" and the "Undo" action are the SAME font size: both use var(--type-body) = 16px (index.html lines 18, 268, 285). The message has no explicit font-weight (inherits body default 400); Undo is explicitly font-weight 500 (line 286) in --color-accent #ed4609 (line 14) against the #1c1c1c card. Equal size but unequal weight+color means Undo carries more visual salience than the message it confirms — a common, arguably intentional pattern for a time-limited affordance (Gmail-style undo toasts put color on the action, not the message), so it is defensible, but a design-exacting reviewer could reasonably ask why the primary confirmation isn't at least as bold as the secondary action rather than plain-weight white next to bold orange.

builds.one_line: A restrained, token-correct dark snackbar with a genuinely defensible confirmation/Undo proportion, undercut by a rest-state Undo that reads as plain text rather than an actionable control.
builds.proportion: Confirmation message ('Change saved') and the Undo action are both rendered at 16px (--type-body via .snackbar-root__message and the inherited .btn font-size) — i.e. IDENTICAL type size, not a scaled-down inline action. The only differentiation is weight: the message inherits body default (400) while .btn sets font-weight:500 (line 108/115). This is defensible for this system — there's no distinct 'small/caption' scale used elsewhere for inline actions (--type-label at 13px is reserved for the eyebrow and status line), and matching size keeps the action legible rather than shrinking it into afterthought territory. It is NOT oversized relative to the message — proportion is sane.

defects.what: At rest, 'Undo' has no color, underline, or icon differentiating it from the plain confirmation text — only a font-weight difference (500 vs ~400) at the same 16px size and same white (#ffffff) color as 'Change saved'. The button only turns visibly interactive (accent #ed4609) on hover, which a mouse-less or glancing user never triggers. Undo is the load-bearing inline action in an optimistic-save pattern and should read as actionable without a hover event.
defects.evidence: .snackbar-root__message has no font-weight declared (line 237-242, inherits ~400); .btn sets font-weight:500 (line 115) — the only rest-state distinction; .btn--ghost color is var(--color-fg, #ffffff) at rest (line 171), identical to the message color

defects.evidence: line 241: .snackbar-root__message { white-space: nowrap; }

defects.what: Undo and Dismiss are both full 44x44 hit targets sitting directly adjacent with only 4px (--space-xs) of declared gap — the accessible tap areas likely touch or nearly touch even though the visible glyphs look comfortably spaced, a mis-tap risk between 'revert' and 'dismiss' actions.
defects.evidence: line 118-119 min-height/min-width:44px on .btn; line 247 gap: var(--space-xs, 4px) inside .snackbar-root__actions

builds.refute_note:
Checked every cited line against the actual CSS/JS and the two renders — all three reviewer defects and the "proportion is sane" claim hold up.

Defect 1 (Undo reads as plain text at rest, medium): confirmed. `.snackbar-root__message` (line 237-242) sets no font-weight, so it inherits the browser default ~400; `.btn` (line 108-129) sets `font-weight:500` explicit and both use the identical `var(--type-body,16px)`. `.btn--ghost` color is `var(--color-fg,#ffffff)` at rest (line 168-174), same white as the message, with only `:hover`/`:active` switching to accent (line 176-182). Zoomed into postsave.png: Undo is very slightly heavier than "Change saved" but there is no border, underline, icon, or color cue — an unhovered, non-mouse user gets essentially no affordance signal beyond a subtle weight bump. This is a real, correctly-evidenced defect; I'd call it borderline low/medium rather than clearly medium, but it's not overturned.

Defect 2 (nowrap, no truncation, low): confirmed at line 241 verbatim. Combined with the fixed `max-width` on `.snackbar-root` (line 208), a long string would overflow the rounded card visually rather than clip cleanly — the reviewer's characterization is accurate.

Defect 3 (44x44 targets with 4px gap, low): confirmed. `.btn` sets `min-height/min-width:44px` (118-119) and neither `.btn--ghost` nor `.btn--icon` overrides that, so both Undo and Dismiss keep full 44px hit boxes; `.snackbar-root__actions` gap is exactly `var(--space-xs,4px)` (line 247). Adjacent 44px targets 4px apart is a legitimate mis-tap risk, correctly low severity.

proportion_verdict re-check: both elements use `var(--type-body,16px)` (lines 114, 238) — identical size confirmed, weight-only differentiation confirmed. Not oversized, not miniaturized. Verdict stands.

One thing the reviewer missed: the 5-second auto-dismiss timer (`AUTO_DISMISS_MS = 5000`, line 285) has no pause-on-hover or pause-on-focus logic anywhere in the script — it only clears on explicit Undo/Dismiss/second-save. For a snackbar whose entire value proposition is a time-boxed Undo action, this is a WCAG 2.2.1 (Timing Adjustable) gap: a slower or motor-impaired user who moves toward the Undo button gets no time extension for lingering there. Worth a low/medium finding the original review didn't surface.

All strengths (token usage, asymmetric padding, motion timing/easing, prefers-reduced-motion override, a11y attributes, ghost-hover-to-accent) check out against the cited lines.

missed.what: Auto-dismiss timer has no pause-on-hover/pause-on-focus; a user reaching toward Undo gets no time extension (WCAG 2.2.1 Timing Adjustable concern) for a component whose whole purpose is a time-boxed reversible action.
missed.evidence: AUTO_DISMISS_MS = 5000 (line 285) and dismissTimer is only cleared by onDismissPressed/onUndoPressed/a fresh save (lines 338, 365, 399) — no mouseenter/mouseleave/focusin/focusout handler exists anywhere in the script.

builds.one_line: Restrained container and solid interaction/motion craft, but the confirmation message is set at heading scale (27px) against a 16px Undo, giving the toast a headline-loud proportion inversion instead of the quiet, compact register a snackbar should hold.
builds.proportion: Confirmation message ("Change saved") is set via .snackbar__message { font-size: var(--type-h3, 27px); font-weight: 400 } (index.html line 222) — the same token size as the page's own h3-scale demo heading. Undo is a plain .btn at font-size: var(--type-body, 16px) with font-weight: 500 (lines 122, 239). Ratio is 27:16 = 1.69x. That is indefensible for this archetype: a snackbar/toast should be a quiet, low-ceremony confirmation, and setting its message at h3/heading scale makes the whole component read as an assertive callout rather than a passing confirmation — it visually competes with the page's own h3 rather than deferring to it, and the box's overall height (~100px at native resolution) is inflated well past a typical 48-56px toast purely because of this oversized type. The Undo action is correctly sized as a compact inline text action on its own terms, but reads as a comparative afterthought next to the oversized message rather than a clear paired action.

defects.what: Confirmation message is set at h3/heading token size (27px), 1.69x the Undo action's 16px, making the toast read as a headline-scale callout instead of a quiet snackbar confirmation.
defects.evidence: .snackbar__message font-size: var(--type-h3, 27px) (index.html line 222) vs .btn font-size: var(--type-body, 16px) (line 122); demo page's own <h1> also uses --type-h3 at 27px (line 74), so the toast message matches the page's actual heading scale.

defects.what: Undo has weak resting-state affordance — it is plain muted-gray text indistinguishable from static copy until hover, with no underline, weight-only differentiation from body text, or accent color to signal it is the load-bearing recovery action.
defects.evidence: .btn--ghost { color: var(--color-fg-muted, #b8b8b8); background: transparent; border-color: transparent } (lines 157-160); only differentiates on :hover/:active (161-162), so the resting postsave.png frame shows Undo as dim gray text with no independent visual cue that it's clickable.

defects.what: Save button's background shifts from pure white (idle) to a light gray in the postsave screenshot, an unexplained residual visual state rather than a clean return to the primary button's default appearance.
defects.evidence: idle.png Save button ~#ffffff vs postsave.png Save button rendering as a light gray fill; .btn--primary default background is var(--color-fg, #ffffff), with only :hover (#b8b8b8) and :active (#828282) as alternates (lines 150-151) — the captured post-save frame appears to be mid-hover/active rather than resting.

defects.what: Snackbar internal padding is asymmetric (16px left, 8px top/right/bottom) which, combined with the oversized 27px/1.2 line-height message, pushes total toast height to roughly double a typical compact toast, undercutting the 'unobtrusive' intent of the archetype.
defects.evidence: padding: var(--space-sm,8px) var(--space-sm,8px) var(--space-sm,8px) var(--space-md,16px) (line 216); message line-height 1.2 at 27px ≈ 32px line box, yielding a toast roughly 96-104px tall including padding+border versus a typical 48-56px snackbar.

builds.refute_note:
Attempted to refute and could not — the reviewer's central claim holds up against both the CSS and the rendered screenshot.

VERIFIED (matches code exactly):
- Line 222: `.snackbar__message { font-size: var(--type-h3, 27px); font-weight: 400 }` — confirmed.
- Line 122: `.btn { font-size: var(--type-body, 16px) }`, applied to `.snackbar__undo` (which only adds `font-weight: 500` at line 239, no size override) — confirmed 16px.
- Ratio 27:16 = 1.6875, reviewer rounded to 1.69x — correct.
- Line 74: `.demo-heading` (the page's own `<h1>`) also uses `--type-h3` at 27px — confirmed the toast message literally matches the demo page's H1 token, exactly as claimed.
- Visually, in postsave.png "Change saved" reads unmistakably headline-scale next to a small "Undo" — this is not a marginal call, it's plainly visible at a glance. The high-severity verdict is well-supported by both code and pixels.
- Medium defect (Undo weak resting affordance): confirmed — `.btn--ghost` (line 156-160) is `color: var(--color-fg-muted)`, `background: transparent`, `border-color: transparent`, differentiated only on `:hover`/`:active` (161-162). Screenshot shows Undo as dim, static-looking gray text. Holds.
- Low defect (asymmetric padding, oversized toast height): `padding: 8px 8px 8px 16px` (line 216) confirmed exactly. Height estimate in the 90-100px range is a reasonable eyeball given 27px text at line-height 1.2 (~32px line box) plus padding/border — holds, though "typical 48-56px toast" is an assumption/convention claim rather than a measured fact.
- Low defect (Save button gray in postsave vs white in idle): confirmed the pixel difference exists (idle white vs postsave light-gray), and the CSS only defines white/hover-gray/active-darker-gray states for `.btn--primary` (150-151) — no other state exists that would explain it. However this is very likely just the cursor still resting on/near the button at capture time (a hover/active artifact of the screenshot script), not a code defect — I'd downgrade this one from "unexplained residual visual state" to "screenshot capture artifact, not a shipped bug." It doesn't change the overall verdict since it's already flagged low-severity.

None of the reviewer's four defects were overturned. The strengths list (state machine, motion asymmetry, reduced-motion override, a11y wiring, actions cleared before exit) are all independently verifiable in the script/CSS and I did not find them exaggerated.

One thing the reviewer didn't call out explicitly but is worth adding: the message's 400 weight next to Undo's 500 weight is a second, smaller inversion — the quiet/secondary action is bolder than the primary confirmation text, compounding (not just size) the proportion problem.

missed.what: Undo is set at font-weight 500 while the primary confirmation message is font-weight 400 — the secondary action is bolder than the primary message, a second small inversion stacking on top of the size inversion.
missed.evidence: index.html line 223 `.snackbar__message { font-weight: 400 }` vs line 239 `.snackbar__undo { font-weight: 500 }`

builds.one_line: Restrained, monochrome snackbar with orange reserved for Undo only — measured proportions are sane and the craft holds up at full resolution.
builds.proportion: Confirmation message ("Change saved") and the Undo action are both set at --type-body: 16px (line 252 for .snackbar__message, line 273 for .snackbar__undo) — a 1:1 size ratio. Undo is differentiated by color (accent #ed4609, line 271) and font-weight 500 rather than by being larger, so it reads as the actionable item without shouting over the confirmation copy — the defensible outcome for a snackbar. defects.evidence: #ed4609 on #1c1c1c computes to ~4.45:1 (relative luminance 0.224 vs 0.0116) — clears the 3:1 large-text/UI-component threshold but sits just under the 4.5:1 normal-text AA threshold Raven's contrast audit would flag

defects.what: Snackbar message uses text-overflow:ellipsis + white-space:nowrap with no max-width guard beyond the 480px snackbar cap
defects.evidence: line 255-257 (.snackbar__message): a longer real-world confirmation string (e.g. a filename) would truncate silently with no title/tooltip fallback

builds.refute_note:
Verified against index.html, idle.png, postsave.png at full resolution. Overall verdict survives; I could not overturn the two strongest defects and found the third overstated but not baseless.

Line-number and color claims checked directly:
- .snackbar__message (line 251-258) and .snackbar__undo (line 267-280) both set font-size: var(--type-body, 16px) — confirmed 1:1 ratio, differentiation is color (#ed4609, line 271) + weight 500 only. Reviewer's proportion read is accurate.
- Contrast math independently re-derived from raw sRGB->linear luminance: #ed4609 on #1c1c1c = ~4.45:1 (L_fg≈0.2241, L_bg≈0.01161, (0.2241+.05)/(0.01161+.05)=4.449). This is CONFIRMED — genuinely fails 4.5:1 AA-normal-text by a hair while clearing 3:1 large-text/UI-component. Reviewer's own luminance figures (0.224 / 0.0116) match my independent calc almost exactly. Not overturned.
- .snackbar__message: white-space:nowrap + text-overflow:ellipsis (lines 255-257) with no `title` attribute set anywhere in the JS (checked index.html script block) — confirmed, a long real string would silently truncate with zero fallback. Not overturned.
- Save-button hover vs active: CONFIRMED the reviewer's wording is overstated. .btn--primary:hover = solid var(--color-accent) (line 169); :active = color-mix(in srgb, accent 80%, black) (line 173) — that resolves to a distinctly darker orange (~rgb(190,56,7) vs rgb(237,70,9)), not visually 'identical.' It's a real but overstated defect: the states ARE differentiated, just by a shade-mix that reads as subtle rather than by any structural change (no border/icon/scale shift) — a legitimate low-severity nit, but 'indistinguishable at a glance' is not accurate language for a ~20% luminance step. I downgraded rather than overturned since the underlying concern (postsave.png only ever shows the hover-orange state, and pressed-state differentiation is genuinely thin) still holds.

Missed, minor, not in the original report:
- On Undo (doUndo), stopTimerBar() only sets transition:none — it does NOT reset transform:scaleX, so during the 1.4s 'Change undone' hold the auto-dismiss hairline is frozen at whatever scaleX the animation had reached rather than resetting to a clean state (index.html script, doUndo/stopTimerBar). Minor visual polish gap, not disqualifying.
- WCAG 2.2.1 (timing adjustable): the 5s auto-dismiss pauses on hover/focus but there is no persistent way to disable/extend it beyond re-triggering hover — an edge a11y nuance the reviewer's a11y strengths bullet (44x44 targets) didn't cover.

Both surviving defects are correctly scored low-severity and don't change ship-readiness; 85 was a fair score but slightly generous given the AA contrast miss is a real, measurable fail (not 'borderline' — it fails) and the active/hover claim needed softening in the other direction. Net: verdict sustained, score nudged to 82.

"Undo" is also 16px (line 277, same --type-body token) but explicitly font-weight:500 (line 278) and colored --color-accent #ed4609 (line 275). Same size, and the secondary action is bolder AND colored while the primary confirmation is plain white/400 — the inline action out-competes the message it should be subordinate to. builds.refute_note:
Verified all four cited defects directly against index.html and both PNGs.

Defect 1 (hierarchy inversion, medium) — MEASUREMENTS ARE CORRECT but the severity/framing is overreach. `.snackbar__message` (line 251) is 16px/inherited-400/white; `.snackbar__undo` (line 277-278) is 16px/500/`--color-accent`. That part is accurately transcribed. But "inverts the intended hierarchy" is a debatable design judgment, not an objective break: bold+colored CTA text on a plain confirmation line is the standard snackbar convention (Gmail's "UNDO", Material snackbar action) precisely because the action is time-limited and clickable while the message is passive information the user already registered by seeing the save happen. The build's own footer explicitly documents this as an intentional choice ("--color-accent marks Undo only"), which cuts against reading it as an oversight. I'd downgrade this to low/stylistic-nitpick, not a medium hierarchy defect blocking ship.

Defect 2 (checkmark icon uses accent too, medium) — CONFIRMED, evidence holds exactly as cited: line 234 `.snackbar__icon { color: var(--color-accent) }` vs footer line 374 claiming accent "marks Undo only, never the surface." This is a genuine self-contradiction in the shipped copy's own stated rule — the one solid medium-severity catch in the review. Keep this one.

Defect 3 (message has no explicit font-weight, low) — CONFIRMED, `.snackbar__message` (250-256) has no weight rule and body sets no base font-weight, so it inherits browser-default 400. Accurately a low-severity consistency gap (every other text role in the file does declare weight explicitly).

Defect 4 (postsave.png button in hover-grey, low) — CONFIRMED by pixel comparison of the two supplied screenshots: idle.png button is pure white (~#ffffff), postsave.png button is light grey matching `--color-fg-muted` #b8b8b8, the documented :hover token (line 160). Capture artifact, correctly flagged as low.

Net: 2 of 4 defects survive as cited; the lead defect driving `ship_ready:false` is a debatable style opinion dressed as a hierarchy break, not a verifiable UX failure — cursor-following bold/colored action text is industry-standard and the build documents it as deliberate. Missed items worth noting: role="status" on the snackbar element nested inside an already aria-live="polite" region is a mild double-announcement risk for screen readers (not in original review); --color-fg-dim sub-line text against --color-bg-elev computes to ~4.6:1 contrast, just barely passing WCAG AA for 13px text — worth a note but not a fail. Overall this is a clean, well-considered build; I'd rate it shippable with the icon/footer contradiction as the one real fix-before-ship item.

builds.one_line: Correct relative hierarchy (message > Undo > dismiss) but the message itself borrows a headline-scale token (27px) that's too loud for a passive, auto-dismissing confirmation.

In isolation that ratio (message clearly larger, inline action clearly subordinate) is the right direction and defensible — but the absolute size chosen for the message (27px, a headline/section-title token) is not defensible for a toast: it's oversized in absolute terms, not just relative to Undo. The Undo/dismiss sizing relative to each other (both 16px) is fine; the message's absolute scale is the actual defect.

That's the same size class used for section headings elsewhere in the scale, so the snackbar reads as a mini page-headline rather than a quiet confirmation. It also outsizes the field value text on the page itself (20px lead), which is backwards for a passive, auto-dismissing element.

builds.refute_note:
Verified the primary high-severity defect directly against index.html and both renders — it holds. Line 282 confirms `.snackbar__message { font-size: var(--type-h3); font-weight: 500; }`, and `--type-h3: 27px` at line 24. Crucially, line 81 shows the demo's own `<h1>` ALSO uses `font-family: var(--font-display); font-size: var(--type-h3); font-weight: 500;` — so the toast confirmation copy is not merely "oversized," it is byte-identical in scale and weight to the page's own headline token. The postsave.png render confirms this visually: "Change saved" reads at essentially the same visual weight as "Optimistic save — snackbar demo" above it. The reviewer's cited outsizing vs. field-value (--type-lead: 20px, line 23 vs 122-126) also checks out exactly. This is a legitimate, well-evidenced high-severity finding, not a stretch — the reviewer even undersold it by not noticing the h1 token match, which strengthens rather than weakens the finding.

The proportion_verdict math is also correct: Undo is --type-body (16px, line 145 via .btn, not overridden by .btn--text) at weight 500 with --color-accent; ratio to the 27px message is 1.69:1, correctly characterized as fine in isolation but built on an oversized absolute base.

I partially overturn the third (low-severity) defect: Undo vs. dismiss differentiation. In the actual render, Undo is rendered in --color-accent (orange #ed4609) against a muted-gray (--color-fg-muted) icon-only dismiss — this is a standard, well-accepted snackbar pattern (Material/GMail-style: color carries the primary/secondary distinction, not size), and the component also has a visual divider (.snackbar__divider) separating message from actions that the reviewer didn't credit. Calling out "no size differentiation beyond color" is technically true but a weak defect — color-only differentiation between a primary text action and a neutral icon-only dismiss is idiomatic, not sloppy. I'd downgrade this to a non-issue rather than a low-severity defect.

The second low-severity defect (snackbar height inflation) is real but is just a restatement/consequence of the first defect, not independently significant — fine as a supporting note but shouldn't be double-counted.

result.critic:
## 1. What would make this comparison unsound

**A single recurring CSS-token bug is doing almost all the work of separating the two groups, not holistic build quality.** Five of the six `ship_ready:false` builds — **03, 06, 07, 09, 12** — share the *identical* high-severity defect: the confirmation message is set to `var(--type-h3, 27px)`, and in every one of the five the refuter independently confirms this is the exact same token the page's own `<h1>`/heading uses (03 line 74 vs 222; 06 line 81 vs 282; 07 line 89 vs 227; 09 line 78 vs 260; 12 line 77 vs 243). The ratio is reported as 1.69x / 27:16 in all five. That's not five independent design judgments converging — that's one templated mistake recurring byte-for-byte, and refute_notes for 06 and 09 say so explicitly ("literally indistinguishable," "byte-identical in scale"). If a tool-keep/delete decision rests on "group B produced worse snackbars," it's actually mostly resting on "group B produced one repeated wrong CSS variable," which is a one-line fix, not a capability gap. Build **05** is the tell: it's in the `false` group but lacks this defect entirely, is scored on a *different, weaker* basis (weight/color hierarchy), and its refute is the one place `refute_sustained` flips to `false` — the odd one out is exactly the build that doesn't share the group's signature bug.

Other confounds visible in the data itself:
- **Self-documenting builds bias the judge with meta-content, not just shipped UI.** Build 08's evidence cites a code comment reading "local component tokens (not in DESIGN.md; defined here, documented in BUILD-LOG)" — the judge is partly grading a build's own narrated rationale, not blind pixels/CSS. Build 05's icon-color defect and defended-hierarchy claim both hinge on the build's own footer text ("--color-accent marks Undo only"). If only one generation method tends to emit this kind of self-annotation, the score partly measures "does this method narrate its own choices," a process artifact, not output quality.
- **No control for whether all 12 builds ran from an identical spec.** Nothing in the record confirms prompt/spec parity within or across the two groups.
- **N=6 per group, one component type only (a snackbar).** No generalization evidence.
- Severity labels aren't decomposed from score — see Q4.

## 2. Where judge and refuter disagree most, and who's better evidenced

**Build-05 is the sharpest break**: judge scored 76/`ship_ready:false` on a "medium" hierarchy-inversion defect (Undo bolder/colored vs. plain message at equal size); refuter is the *only* one to set `refute_sustained: false` and pushes the score to 84 — actually higher than the lowest `ship_ready:true` judge score (build-01/02 at 83).

The refuter is better evidenced here, and it's not just a difference of opinion — it's an **internal-consistency catch**. The exact same pattern (message and Undo at identical 16px, differentiated only by weight+color) is explicitly treated as *defensible/standard* in the proportion_verdicts of builds **01** ("arguably intentional Gmail-style"), **04** ("the defensible outcome for a snackbar"), **08** ("matching common snackbar conventions... Material/Base UI"), and **10** ("avoiding the common snackbar mistake of an oversized bold CTA"). The judge on 05 penalized the identical pattern as a medium defect while the corpus's own judges waved it through elsewhere — the refuter caught the inconsistency and cited the build's own footer plus industry convention to overturn it. That's a well-grounded reversal, not a coin flip.

Second-largest gap: **build-11**, sustained but cut 85→78 (7 points, the largest within-"sustained" delta in the set). The refuter invokes a real project rule — Andrew's own "no hardcoded CSS values, always use tokens" — against the 11px literal (line 261), says outright "I'd argue this alone is enough to make me hesitant to rubber-stamp ship_ready at 85," then adds a missed WCAG 2.2.1 timing gap on top — yet leaves `ship_ready:true` unchanged despite its own stated discomfort. That's a real, well-evidenced downgrade whose verdict label doesn't track its own prose.

## 3. Is within-group spread large enough that the between-group gap could be noise?

Yes — concretely:

| | judge scores | range | refute scores | range |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `ship_ready:true` (N=6): 01,02,04,08,10,11 | 83,83,85,85,87,85 | **4 pts** (83–87) | 83,81,82,83,85,**78** | **7 pts** (78–85) |
| `ship_ready:false` (N=6): 03,05,06,07,09,12 | 64,**76**,64,60,72,64 | **16 pts** (60–76) | 63,**84**,64,58,76,63 | **26 pts** (58–84) |

Before refutation, the closest-group gap is 83 (true-floor) − 76 (false-ceiling, build-05) = **7 points** — smaller than the false-group's own internal spread (16 points). After the adversarial pass, the groups **invert**: build-05 refutes to **84**, which is *higher* than build-11's refuted **78** — the lowest-scoring member of the `true` group now scores below the highest-scoring member of the `false` group. With N=6 per group and a between-group margin this thin relative to within-group variance (and one clean inversion under adversarial correction), the raw true/false split is not robust — at minimum builds 05 and 11 are statistically indistinguishable once severity judgments are corrected.

## 4. What measurement is missing

The decisive missing measurement is an **ablation/counterfactual**: patch `--type-h3` → `--type-body` on the message in builds 03, 06, 07, 09, 12 (the one line each time), re-render, re-score blind. If the group gap collapses to noise once that single token is fixed, the comparison was measuring one bug, not two build methods. Nothing in the current data tells you this.

Also missing:
- **A disclosed scoring rubric** — is a single "high" defect an automatic `ship_ready:false` regardless of everything else? (09's refute_note says exactly that: "the high-severity type-scale issue alone still justifies ship_ready:false" — i.e., one item is deciding the boolean.)
- **A cross-build diff of the message-CSS block** in 03/06/07/09/12 to see if it's literally identical text (shared-template leakage) vs. independently generated.
- **Independent second raters**, blind to each other and to the judge's citations — every refute_note here re-verifies the judge's own line numbers rather than conducting a from-scratch pass, so judge and refuter errors are correlated, not independent.
- **A human/eyes-on ground truth** (Andrew's own taste read) to anchor the two LLM passes against something non-machine.
- **Rule for whether refute_score should recompute `ship_ready`** — build-05's refuted 84 sits inside the "true" range but its `ship_ready` field was never flipped.

## 5. Signs judges weren't actually blind

No verdict names a build method, arm, "prompt type," or otherwise states provenance directly — I found no literal "Build A/B" or "spec-driven vs freeform" leakage in any judge or refuter text.

Two adjacent concerns, though:
- **Builds narrate their own design intent inline** (05's footer: "--color-accent marks Undo only, never the surface"; 08's code comment citing "documented in BUILD-LOG"), and judges lean on that self-narration as evidence. A judge citing "the build's own footer explicitly documents this as intentional" is being informed by authorial commentary baked into the artifact — which is a channel for method-identity to leak through the artifact itself, even to a nominally blind judge, if only one generation approach tends to produce that kind of inline rationale.
- **Highly repetitive "missed" findings across builds** (near-identical WCAG 2.2.1 "auto-dismiss has no pause-on-hover/focus" language independently surfacing in builds 02, 09, 10, 11) suggest the refuter is running a fixed mental checklist per build rather than a build-specific fresh audit each time — not a blindness break, but it does mean the "independently found" defects are less independent than they look, and shouldn't be over-weighted as corroboration.
